passage: I'm Vasudha. Since I was ten, everyone knew I'd join our family's accounts firm; my grandfather's name is painted on the board over the door. When the careers counsellor handed out interest quizzes in Class 11, I didn't fill mine in. "No need," I told Parul, my desk-mate. "Commerce, then the firm." I said it with total certainty, people nodded, and that felt solid, like standing on a floor. Parul filled in hers twice and changed her mind three times. I felt sorry for her. But lately, when I sit in the firm on Saturdays sorting files, I feel nothing much. Not unhappy. Just flat, like a song with the volume turned down. I've never tested any other door. I'm starting to wonder whether that certainty was ever mine.

qa.a: Vasudha's grandfather's name.

passage: Counsellor's note, 22 July. Written by Aparna. Akash, fifteen, came in for the Class 10 stream session. When I asked what he wanted, he answered before I finished: "Army. Like my father and both uncles. It's decided." He smiled, but the smile didn't reach his eyes, and he spoke like someone reading a timetable. I asked what else he had considered. He looked puzzled. "Nothing. Why would I?" I asked what he enjoys most in school. He took a long time, then said, "Biology practicals, maybe." He said it quietly, almost like a secret. I did not challenge the army plan; it may well suit him. I have suggested he spend a week of the summer shadowing a lab and talk it over with his father. Follow-up on 5 August.

Saturday, 10 pm
Paati's concert anniversary today. Everyone said it again: "Nandini will carry the family's voice." I sang the varnam without one slip and Amma cried a little and called me her good girl. I'm going to be a singer like Paati. That's settled; it has been since I was six.
At lunch Sunaina asked me to try the robotics club with her, just once. I said no need, I already know what I'm doing with my life. She looked at me funny. "But do you like it?" I said obviously.
Obviously. I've written that word and now I'm staring at it.
When I practise, it's fine. I'm good at it. I don't hate it. I don't feel much of anything, actually, which is probably normal.
Whatever. Practice at six tomorrow.
Nandini
